text: Hey everybody, I'm Dan McClellan. I'm a
scholar of the Bible and religion and in
my previous video I shared that I was
wearing my Adonai and his Asherah
t-shirt and I had a number of folks ask
what was going on on this t-shirt and
who was being depicted. And this is a
drawing that comes from my favorite
artifact from the ancient world. It
comes from a place called Kuntillet
Ajrud, which is located in the Sinai
Peninsula and it depicts the god of
Israel and God's consort partner or wife
Asherah, at least according to the
inscription that is centered over the
headdress on the male figure. This
version of the shirt doesn't show that
inscription, but I have another version
that does show that part of the
inscription and these shirts and many
others are available on either of the
two Data Over Dogma stores that I have
linked to in my link tree if you want to
go check out what I have there. But I
also happen to have a life-size replica
of this artifact and here it is and you
can see the male and the female figure
and the inscription that is centered
over the male's headdress. And this is a
drawing and inscription that comes from
a large jar called a pithos. This is
pithos A from Kuntillet Ajrud and there
are other drawings and inscriptions from
other parts of this pithos, but this one
I find most fascinating. It represents a
male and a female figure who show uh
imagery associated with the Egyptian
deity Bes and a female counterpart
Beset. And while some people think the
drawings are supposed to just represent
that Egyptian deity,
we know that in this time and place it
was not uncommon to overlay such imagery
on other deities in order to kind of
assign the features associated with Bes
and Beset to other deities. And the
inscription that is written over top of
the male figure and centered above the
male's headdress refers to blessings by
Adonai and by his Asherah. And this is a
wonderful paper written by a friend of
mine named Ryan Thomas that discusses
why it is most likely that we should
identify the male and the female
standing figures in this pithos as
Adonai and his Asherah and I and many
other scholars understand this to be
pretty secure evidence that around 800
BCE, prior to the reign of Josiah,
toward the end of the 7th century BCE,
the worship of Adonai alongside a
consort partner or wife was pretty
common. There does not seem to be any
kind of institutional opposition to it
until we get to Josiah. In other words,
God had a wife prior to the late 7th
century BCE. And obviously a bunch of
people are going to respond that no,
that is just the apostate Israelites.
Those are the people who were
backsliding into idolatry and were doing
what they knew wasn't right. However,
that's not really supported by the data
because the earliest evidence of any
kind that we have that Asherah was
demonized or vilified or her worship was
prohibited comes from the time of Josiah
in the late 7th century BCE. And so we
can't just presuppose that the
prohibitions and the ideals that were
asserted in this campaign of cult
centralization on Josiah's part toward
the end of the 7th century BCE can be
retrojected further back into Israel's
history. Most scholars who study early
Israelite religion agree that from the
very beginning, all the way down
probably to around Josiah, it wasn't
considered a big deal that Adonai had a
consort partner or wife. Now, originally
it would have been the wife of El, the
Northwest Semitic patriarchal high
deity, who originally was likely
distinct from the youthful warrior storm
deity divine profile that was
appropriated by Adonai when they were
brought into the central or northern
hill country. But probably somewhere
around 1000 BCE, the divine profiles of
Adonai and of El were conflated and the
two deities became one. And from then
on, El's consort partner or wife became
Adonai's consort partner or wife until
Josiah's campaign of cult centralization
literally demonized and vilified Asherah
and prohibited her worship. So I think
this is one of the most fascinating
archaeological discoveries about ancient
Israel. It's my favorite artifact from
the ancient world. My friend Robert
Algot made this
replica, which surprised me how big it
was. I have never seen the original in
person, but I wasn't aware of precisely
how big it was. And I love being able to
tell people who ask what's going on on
my t-shirt that that is an ancient
Israelite drawing of God and their wife.
And the fit for this video obviously
continues to be Adonai and his Asherah.
